gui.eternal_defense.guide.start.body:
# What is this mod about?
- Monsters attack your base in big raids. You plant a Defense Beacon, build around it and protect it.
- Win a raid and you get prizes. Spend them to get stronger. Then a bigger raid comes. Repeat.
- On the way you get guns, ammo tables, a kitchen, a support cannon and more. Each has its own page in this book.
# Your first steps
- Step 1: Look in your pack. You already have a Defense Beacon, this book, a Recovery Shovel and a starter gun.
- Step 2: Choose where to plant the beacon. Read the red notes below first!
- Step 3: Right-click the ground with the beacon, read the screen, then press Plant beacon.
- Step 4: A short first raid starts AT ONCE. Hold your gun, keep your ammo handy and stay close to the beacon.
- Step 5: Win it. You earn a Weapon Platform and your campaign is rolling.

# Defense Beacon
- What it is: A glowing crystal in the heart of your base. There is one per world, in the Overworld, and the whole team shares it.
- You get: A protected zone to build in, raids to fight and prizes for every win.
- How it works: Right-click it to open its screen: Overview, Upgrades, Workshop Fabrication and Raid control. Settings and this Guide are in the header.
- How to unlock: You start with one in your pack.
- Careful: The beacon cannot be broken or moved. Only the Recovery Shovel removes it, and that RESETS the whole campaign: every upgrade, win and reward tier goes back to zero. Your buildings stay.
- Careful: So choose the spot well, and leave clear space around it (see Your base zone).
- Careful: Wild monsters can hit an exposed beacon too if they can see it from 24 blocks away. Cover it with solid blocks. During a raid cover no longer hides it: every monster within 48 blocks of your zone comes for it.

# Recovery Shovel
- What it is: A special iron shovel. It is also your remote control for the beacon.
- You get: The beacon's control panel from far away, a status display while you hold it, free moving of your support gear, and a way to push enemies back.
- How it works: Right-click the air to open the panel. Hit a monster to knock it back (it does no damage). Use it on your Support Platform or Cannon to pick it up. Use it on the beacon to pack the campaign up.
- How to unlock: You start with one. Lost it? Craft a new one at a crafting table: iron above and below, copper left and right, redstone in the middle.
- Careful: Using it on the beacon is the reset button. The game asks you to confirm first.

# Field Guide
- What it is: This book.
- You get: Answers while you play.
- How it works: Right-click it to open. Pick a page from the list, or use Back and Next or the arrow keys. Scroll with the mouse wheel.
- How to unlock: You start with one. Lost it? Craft paper and a copper ingot together.

# Starter gun
- What it is: A basic gun and some ammo, so you can fight the very first raid.
- You get: One .22 Model 943 revolver and 64 rounds of .22 WMR for it.
- How it works: The revolver holds 8 rounds. Press {reload} to reload it.
- How to unlock: You get it once, the first time you join the world.
- Careful: You only get one. Ammo you spend stays spent, so make your shots count.
gui.eternal_defense.guide.start.detail:
- The introductory raid is fixed at tier 0.
- Raids that follow come faster as your reward tier improves, down to one every three active days.
gui.eternal_defense.guide.zone.body:
# Your base zone
- What it is: The area around the beacon that is yours. A moving cyan grid shows its edges, even above and below you.
- You get: A safe home for your kitchen, Exchange Shop and support gear. They can only be placed inside it. Weapon tables inside it also raise your base score.
- How it works: At first it reaches 8 blocks each way from the beacon. Core upgrades make it wider. Vertical upgrades make it taller.
- How to unlock: It appears the moment you plant the beacon.
- Careful: It is centred on the beacon and never moves unless the beacon does. Leave a clear 3 x 3 space, two blocks tall, around the beacon, or the biggest Core upgrade (Mk-4) cannot be built.
- Good to know: You can switch the grid off in Settings.
- Good to know: Hold one of this mod's blocks and look at the ground: a see-through copy shows where it would stand. It turns red when a block or a creature is in the way. Then it is not placed and you keep it.

# Base score and rewards
- What it is: A grade for your base. The beacon looks at what you built inside the zone.
- You get: A better base earns better prizes after every raid (reward tier 0 to 10). Overview shows your score.
- How it works: Walls, roofs and rooms you place count. Extra points for mixed materials, details (stairs, slabs, fences, doors), lights, furniture (beds, bookshelves, barrels, chests, tables) and closed rooms you can use.
- How to unlock: Nothing to unlock. Just build.
- Careful: A higher reward tier means bigger raids that come more often: every 10 days at tier 0, down to every 3 days. You can hold them back in Raid control.
- Careful: Natural terrain gives nothing, and ore blocks are worth no more than plain blocks.
- Good to know: Each of this mod's installations standing in your zone adds 25 points (Installations on the Overview). All 20 together add 500, one whole reward tier.

# Settings
- What it is: Three switches in the header of the beacon screen.
- You get: The cyan zone grid, the sky beam and a red box showing the part of the beacon enemies can actually hurt.
- How it works: Click a switch to turn it on or off. The beam is shared by the whole team.
- How to unlock: Always there.
- Good to know: The Settings tab also has Idle animations. Switch it off and flags, dishes and flames stand still; only you see the change.
gui.eternal_defense.guide.zone.detail:
- Core upgrades give Mk-2, Mk-3 and Mk-4 with zone radii 12, 20 and 32 blocks (65 blocks across at Mk-4, as wide as the tallest zone is tall). Vertical upgrades raise the height separately, up to 16 below and 48 above, without changing HP or the model.
- The cyan lines sit on the OUTER faces of the included blocks. One-block ticks help you count, and corners count too.
- A separate red outline in Settings shows the part of the beacon that enemies can damage. It starts three blocks below and eight above.
- Existing crafted blocks are recognized. Occupied, covered rooms also credit raw stone and dirt.
- Stations inside the zone add score. Only the highest Age of each of the four station types counts: 40 / 90 / 180 / 300 / 450 for Ages 1 to 5.
- Rewards & tiers previews the exact shared payouts, including wave iron and hard-raid bonuses.
- Build Create machines, turrets and Universal Platforms inside the zone. Factories and higher station Ages boost your score.
- Installations (25 points each, 500 for all 20): Exchange Shop, Support Platform, Support Cannon, the Weapon, Ammo, Attachment and Armor Platforms, Mess Hall, Cook Pot, Bowl Dispenser, Milk Dispenser, Drink Station, Brew Pot, Cup Dispenser, MRE Station, Logistics Center Hub, Command Table, Satellite Beacon, Supply Receiving Gate and Tactical Enchanting Table. A Mess Hall or Drink Station counts once, whatever its Mk.
gui.eternal_defense.guide.raids.body:
# Raids
- What it is: Waves of monsters that march on your beacon to wreck it.
- You get: A cache of prizes and Ardent Energy for winning. Everything the raiders broke is put back.
- How it works: Raiders appear outside your zone and march on the beacon. Each has a red "!" above its head. Kill every one to win. Any left alive start to glow after 5 minutes, sooner with Reconnaissance.
- How to unlock: Plant the beacon. A short first raid starts at once. After that raids come only at night: every 10 active days at reward tier 0, one day sooner per tier (down to every 3 days). The clock counts ACTIVE days, so it stops while nobody is online.
- Careful: If three defenders die near the beacon, the beacon loses health. The skull on its health bar counts the deaths it can still take. If it is overrun you lose, and the damage stays until you repair it.
- Good to know: On the way, raiders go for the closest defense in their path first, like a turret, and break closed doors and gates. Then fighters rush the beacon. They hit it from any block around it, or from on top.
- Good to know: Fighters only turn on you when you come close. Archers and gunners shoot at you first and the beacon after. Raiders ignore players in Creative.
- Good to know: Raiders dig through walls block by block, and you can watch the cracks grow. Tough blocks take longer, and raiders dig faster together. A creeper near your base blows the wall up instead.
- Good to know: Raiders lay plank bridges across water, lava and chasms. Raiders that come later walk a bridge already there and lay on from its end. Break a bridge to drop them in. The raid takes every bridge away when it ends.
- Good to know: A raider stuck for a long time stands still for about 8 seconds beside a red gate, then steps out of a second red gate just outside your zone. You can shoot it while it waits.
- Good to know: A raider in deep water goes to a red gate at once when it would need more than 5 seconds to swim to land, or after 5 seconds in the water.
- Careful: Raiders never give up. After three gates, or when your beacon sits high above them, stuck raiders join the parachute squadron and drop right above the beacon. Chat says so.
- Good to know: Enemies come in from open ground far outside your zone, with a burst of speed. Where there is none (forest, water, mountains), they come out of red gates closer in, never inside the zone. Chat says so once a wave.
- Good to know: With no ground at all around your base, enemies jump by parachute over your zone instead.
- Good to know: Raids have their own music. Every wave starts a new song that has not played yet in that raid, and its name shows under the beacon card. Winning plays a fanfare. Turn either off in the beacon's Settings tab.

# Warnings
- What it is: Messages that tell you a raid is coming.
- You get: Time to get home and get ready.
- How it works: Chat warns you about a day ahead, then every six hours, then once more when the raid is only waiting for night. Big banners show the start, each wave, VICTORY and DEFEAT. A red BEACON IS BEING ATTACKED warning reaches every player, in any dimension.
- How to unlock: Nothing to do. They are always on.

# Hard raids and bosses
- What it is: Every third raid is a hard raid: simply a stronger raid with a boss. It has nothing to do with how often raids come.
- You get: A bigger prize, with a bonus on top.
- How it works: 25%% more attackers, and a boss walks in with the final wave. Beating the boss pays 50%% more completion rewards.
- How to unlock: It happens by itself. Overview tells you when the next raid is a hard one.
- Careful: Get ready for these. The boss is much tougher than the rest.
- Good to know: The boss is a modded boss with a red boss bar. Beating it also gives bonus medical kits and grenades.

# Elite mobs
- What it is: Raid mobs with a special power. A glowing ring in the power's colour turns at their feet and a red health bar floats over their head, so you can spot them at night too. Their name shows in gold, or red for the toughest.
- You get: Every elite drops Ardent Energy when it dies, the tough ones more. Every wave with an elite adds 1 Ardent Energy to the raid's pay. Chat says so when one shows up.
- How it works: Low raid levels bring at least one elite in the whole raid, the first raid too. From level 5 there is one in every wave, and at level 10 about three a wave. The Elite Cadre modifier adds one more a wave.
- How to unlock: Automatic in every raid. In the first raid a Badass is always level I.
- Careful: Read the name before you fight. Some explode or split when they die.
- Badass I to V: much more health (four times as much at I, sixteen times at V) and a bigger body, up to a giant five times as big. From Badass II on, a stuck giant smashes through walls. The bigger it is, the slower it walks. A Badass creeper is even slower, but its blast grows with its size. Higher levels are rarer.
- Speedster: twice the rush speed of other raid mobs, and it keeps it until it dies.
- Healer: heals every hostile mob near it, raid mob or not.
- Matrioska: half the health, but it explodes when killed and two copies take its place. The copies split once more.
- Long Shot: an archer that shoots from five times as far, very straight, with arrows that explode and break blocks.
- Flak Armor: 50%% more health. Explosions do only 40%% damage, bullets and melee 20%% more.
- Body Armor: 50%% more health. Bullets do only 40%% damage, explosions and melee 20%% more.
- Vampiric: 50%% more health, and it heals itself by half the damage it deals.
- Frostbite: 50%% more health, and its hits slow you down and slow your digging.
- Berserker: 50%% more health, and it hits harder the more hurt it is, up to twice as hard.
- Only mobs that fight up close become Vampiric, Frostbite or Berserker. Only archers become a Long Shot.

# Special Forces
- What it is: Soldiers with guns who join raids once your reward tier is 4 or more.
- You get: Loot. Their bodies can be looted for about ten minutes after they fall.
- How it works: You get a warning first. Get behind sandbags and shoot it out. You meet one soldier per wave at tiers 4 to 6, and heavy soldiers from tier 7.
- How to unlock: Automatic once you reach tier 4.
- Careful: They shoot back from far away. Stay behind cover.

# Trap learning
- What it is: Raiders get used to the same trap again and again.
- You get: A good reason to mix your defenses.
- How it works: Each trap type hurts in full during the first wave. After that raiders take 25%% less from it every wave, until it does nothing after four steps. Chat tells you when they adapt. It starts over with the next raid.
- How to unlock: Automatic.
- Careful: Raiders are protected from sunlight only. Flame arrows and fire traps still work, but do not rely on one kind of trap. Turrets, guns, your own projectiles and your support cannon never get weaker.

# Winning and losing
- Win: Everything the raiders broke is put back. Your prizes go to the beacon's reward chest.
- Lose: The beacon is switched off and the damage stays. Repair it from Overview (see Repair or pack up).
- Careful: Spent ammo, fuel and tool wear are never refunded, win or lose.

# Reward chest
- What it is: The beacon itself. It is the chest that holds your prizes.
- You get: A 54-slot chest for the whole team, so loot stays out of your pack.
- How it works: Press Reward chest in Overview. New prizes are put in each time you open it, and whatever does not fit waits in a queue.
- How to unlock: It is there as soon as the beacon is planted.
- Careful: If the beacon is ever destroyed, what is inside spills out. If you pack the campaign up with the shovel, unclaimed prizes are thrown away, so empty the chest first.
gui.eternal_defense.guide.raids.detail:
- Ordinary enemies have bounded health and no armor. Specialists have light armor, and marked heavies are uncommon.
- Special Forces begin at reward tier 4. Solo tiers 4 to 6 send one soldier per wave; heavies start at tier 7. When warned, get behind sandbags for a shootout.
- Downed Special Forces count as defeated, and their bodies stay lootable for up to ten active minutes.
- Extra nearby Survival or Adventure defenders raise reinforcement counts by 65%% each, not enemy health. The count locks at each wave and shows in Overview. Alive-enemy limits are 24 solo and 48 in co-op. Spectators, Creative players and distant players do not count.
- Veteran victories add at most 30%% reinforcements, with no hidden health growth. Boss health adds 45%% per extra defender, up to four.
- Defeats still count toward the three-raid cadence. Every raid after the first starts at night, even one you start yourself.
- The reward chest needs two adjacent ground-level blocks clear with headroom, at least three blocks from the beacon, inside the zone. Create the first one between raids. Its 54 slots keep supplies out of your inventory.
- Higher reward tiers shorten the next interval: 10, 9, 8, 7, 6, 5, 4, then 3 days.
- Elites: below raid level 5, one wave of the raid always has one, and every wave has a 20%% chance a level (40%% at level 2). Level 5 brings 1 a wave, then 0.4 more a level, 3 at level 10.
- Elite drops: 1 Ardent Energy, 2 for a Healer, Matrioska or Long Shot, and the Badass level for a Badass. A Matrioska's copies drop none of their own.
- Badass levels: I to V in 40, 25, 17, 11 and 7 odds. The top level is 1 plus half the raid level (V from level 8). Sizes by level: 1.5, 2.2, 3, 4 and 5 times; a bigger one also climbs higher.
- Badass speed: 2.5%% slower a level (12.5%% at V); a creeper 3.75%% a level (18.75%% at V). A Badass creeper's blast radius: 5, 7, 9, 12 and 15 blocks (a plain creeper's is 3).
- Elite ring colours (the health bar is always red): Badass gold, red from IV; Speedster yellow; Healer green; Matrioska pink; Long Shot sky blue; Flak Armor silver; Body Armor bronze; Vampiric crimson; Frostbite ice blue; Berserker orange.
- Defenses in the way: within 16 blocks of a raider and closer to it than the beacon, no farther from the beacon than the raider plus 4 blocks, at most 6 blocks up or down. A raider that cannot hurt one for 20 seconds leaves it alone for a minute.
- Digging: a block takes 3 damage plus 6 per point of hardness, 300 at most (dirt 6, planks and cobblestone 15, obsidian 300). A raider swings twice a second for half its attack damage, a giant more. Arrows and bullets do 3 to a defense or door. Cracks heal after 8 seconds.
- Players: fighters turn on a player within 4 blocks (3 up or down) and let go past 10 blocks. Archers and gunners take a player they can see within 32 blocks and keep on them within 40 blocks for 10 seconds after they last saw them.
- Bridges: over water and lava, and over falls of 3 blocks or more when the land comes back at the same height or the target is not lower. Up to 24 planks a bridge and 384 a raid. A raider at the edge uses a bridge of the raid that starts within 16 blocks and leads toward its target: it walks to it, crosses, and lays up to 24 more planks from its end.
- Water: a raider swimming (head under water, or off the ground) goes to a gate when the water toward its target before land would take more than 5 seconds at its best swimming speed (a zombie: about 0.37 blocks a second, so 2 blocks of water or more), or once it has been in the water for 5 seconds. Drowned and water mobs swim on.
- Squadron: a raider that made no progress for 25 seconds opens a gate. After 3 gates, 3 tries without a place, or 4 blocks or more below the beacon within 8 blocks of the zone, it jumps from 24 blocks above the beacon.
gui.eternal_defense.guide.control.body:
# Raid level cap
- What it is: A dial from 0 to 10 that limits how hard raids can get.
- You get: Easier raids while you are still weak. The cap limits both the enemies and the prizes.
- How it works: Open the Raid control tab, then Level & break. Press - or + beside the cap. The big line under it shows the level the next raid is fought at, and below it its waves, mobs, elites and pay. Your base score and upgrades are not touched.
- How to unlock: Always there.
- Careful: The whole team shares this dial, and a low cap means smaller prizes.

# Start raid
- What it is: Do not want to wait for the countdown? Start the raid yourself.
- You get: A raid at the level shown, with its prizes, at a time you choose.
- How it works: Press Start raid at the bottom of Raid control. At night it starts at once; by day it starts when night falls. The base is saved first. Any break you bought ends. Every third raid still has a boss.
- How to unlock: Always there.
- Careful: Once it starts you cannot take it back. Check that everyone is ready.

# Raid break
- What it is: Pay to push the next raid back.
- You get: Five days of peace per purchase, so you can go on long trips. Buy more and they add up.
- How it works: Open Raid control, then Level & break, and press Buy five active days. Each purchase costs more than the last. Only days when someone is online count.
- How to unlock: Always there. The price is shown above the button.
- Careful: Every break also makes your NEXT raid tougher and richer (up to 3 tiers higher, never above your cap). Wild monsters still attack an exposed beacon during a break.
- Break price: brass, precision mechanisms and gold.

# Raid modifiers
- What it is: Extra dangers you add to the next raid, on the Raid modifiers page of Raid control.
- You get: A bigger prize. Each one makes the raid's cache bigger and makes raid mobs drop Ardent Energy more often. The page shows how much. All of them and a special raid together make raid mobs drop it twice as often as the base chance.
- How it works: Switch on any number of them, between raids, near the beacon. They count for the next raid only, whether you press Start raid or its timer runs out. When it starts, the switches go back off.
- How to unlock: After the first raid.
- Careful: They add up, and so does the danger. The whole team fights the raid you pick.
- Reinforcements: 30%% more mobs every wave.
- Elite Cadre: one more elite every wave.
- Hardened: raid mobs have 35%% more health.
- Forced March: raid mobs move 20%% faster.
- Fog of War: switches off your Reconnaissance upgrade for that raid. Mobs left alive never glow through walls.
- Exposed Beacon: mobs that hit the beacon do 50%% more damage to it.

# Special raids
- What it is: A raid with a twist that you choose: Air raid, Paratroopers, Siege or Thousands.
- You get: Extra Ardent Energy when you win it, and raid mobs drop Ardent Energy more often.
- How it works: On the Raid modifiers page, pick one in the Special raid row, or Ordinary for none. Only one at a time, on top of any modifiers.
- How to unlock: After the first raid. Every raid is ordinary unless someone picks one.
- Air raid: flying mobs ignore walls. You need anti-air, not thicker walls.
- Paratroopers: heavy mobs drop in on red parachutes. Shoot them while they float.
- Siege: creepers blow holes in your walls and shooters fire through the holes.
- Thousands: only zombies, in huge swarms. Bring lots of ammo.
- Careful: Build the right counter before it starts.
gui.eternal_defense.guide.control.detail:
- Purchases add up to three bonus tiers within your chosen cap.
- The next started raid uses the bonus and resets the purchase price.
- Starting a raid saves a snapshot of the base first. Ambient enemies stay active during a break.
- Raid modifiers (payout, Ardent drops as a percent of the base chance): Reinforcements +20%% and +8%%, Elite Cadre +15%% and +9%%, Hardened +15%% and +8%%, Forced March +10%% and +6%%, Fog of War +10%% and +5%%, Exposed Beacon +15%% and +6%%. The payout bonus raises every stack of the cache, rounded up.
- A special raid adds 8%% to the Ardent drops (with every modifier, 50%% in all: twice the base chance) and pays its own Ardent bonus: 4 at level 0, 17 at level 5 and 29 at level 10.
gui.eternal_defense.guide.upgrades.body:
# How upgrades work
- What it is: Permanent boosts for the whole base, in six branches.
- You get: A bigger zone, better prizes, a tougher beacon and more.
- How it works: Right-click the beacon and open Upgrades. Each card shows what you hold and what it costs. Press Buy. Do it near the beacon, between raids.
- How to unlock: The tab is always there. In Creative mode everything is free.
- Careful: Packing up the beacon with the shovel wipes every upgrade.
- Making the parts: JEI shows the Create recipes for each upgrade component. Make enough, carry them, then buy. Hover a material icon: {jei}

# Core
- What it is: The beacon's own strength, Mk-1 to Mk-4.
- You get: A wider zone and a tougher beacon with every level.
- How it works: There are three Core upgrades. Each grows the zone and the beacon's health.
- How to unlock: Buy it in the Upgrades tab.
- Careful: Mk-4 needs a clear 3 x 3 space, two blocks tall, around the beacon.

# Logistics
- What it is: Your supply lines. This is how you earn better prizes.
- You get: Each of its five levels adds one reward tier. A good base adds up to five more. Tier 10 is the top.
- How it works: A higher tier means bigger prizes after every raid.
- How to unlock: Buy it in the Upgrades tab.
- Careful: A higher reward tier also makes raids bigger and brings them more often. Lower the cap in Raid control if you need a breather.

# Defense
- What it is: Armor for the beacon.
- You get: 15, 30, 45 and 60%% less damage to the beacon, in four levels.
- How it works: Everything that hits the beacon does less damage.
- How to unlock: Buy it in the Upgrades tab.

# Restoration
- What it is: A repair crew.
- You get: Faster rebuilding after a raid, and the beacon heals 5, 10, 15, 20 and then 25%% of its health after a victory.
- How it works: It works by itself once bought.
- How to unlock: Buy it in the Upgrades tab.

# Vertical zone
- What it is: A taller base zone.
- You get: More room above and below, up to 16 blocks down and 48 up.
- How it works: It only changes the height. The beacon's health and model stay the same.
- How to unlock: Buy it in the Upgrades tab.
- Good to know: It takes some of all four parts: 2 of each at first, then 4, 8 and 16.

# Reconnaissance
- What it is: A scout.
- You get: Attackers glow sooner, so you see them through walls: after 3 minutes, then 1 minute, then from the moment each wave starts. Without it they glow after 5 minutes.
- How it works: Three levels. Each one makes them glow sooner.
- How to unlock: Buy it in the Upgrades tab.
gui.eternal_defense.guide.repair.body:
# Repair
- What it is: The fix for a beacon that a raid switched off.
- You get: +250 health and the campaign restarts.
- How it works: Open the beacon, go to Overview and press Repair. The button shows the price.
- How to unlock: The button shows up when the beacon is switched off.
- Careful: Repairs never refund ammo or fuel you spent.
- Good to know: Park and disassemble moving Create contraptions before raids.

# Pack up and reset
- What it is: The way to stop the whole campaign.
- You get: One fresh Defense Beacon back, ready to plant somewhere else.
- How it works: Hold the Recovery Shovel near the beacon and use it on the beacon, or use Settings > Remove. Read the screen, then confirm.
- How to unlock: Always possible, but you need the shovel within 8 blocks.
- Careful: Raids stop and ALL upgrades, wins and reward tiers go back to zero. Unclaimed prizes are thrown away. Your buildings stay.
- Careful: This affects every player on the world. Talk to your team first.
gui.eternal_defense.guide.stations.body:
# Weapon Platform
- What it is: The gun shop. A big workbench for guns.
- You get: Any gun you have unlocked, made from materials. Search by name and filter by type and era.
- How it works: Open it with empty hands. Pick a gun, check the materials and press Craft.
- How to unlock: Win the first raid to claim yours. Buy more at Workshop Fabrication.
- Careful: Guns from later eras are locked until the table is upgraded. A locked gun shows what it needs.

# Ammo Platform
- What it is: The ammo shop. It only shows ammo that fits the gun in your hand.
- You get: Bullets and empty magazines.
- How it works: Hold your gun and right-click the table, or press {interact} while looking at it. Pick the ammo and pay with materials or with Ammo Coins.
- How to unlock: Buy it at Workshop Fabrication.
- Careful: A magazine you craft here is EMPTY. Fill it with your loose rounds using the magazine addon. Coins buy empty magazines, never filled ones.

# Attachment Platform
- What it is: The attachment shop: scopes, grips, extended magazines and more. It only shows parts that fit the gun in your hand.
- You get: Upgrades for your gun.
- How it works: Hold your gun and right-click the table, or press {interact} while looking at it.
- How to unlock: Buy it at Workshop Fabrication.
- Careful: Some parts need a later Age. The list counts how many are still locked.

# Armor Platform
- What it is: The armor shop: helmets, vests, leg protection, boots, pouches, plates and vision gear.
- You get: Protection and extra carrying room.
- How it works: Open it with empty hands.
- How to unlock: Buy it at Workshop Fabrication.
- Good to know: It always makes the five Age Armor Sets. Armor from other armor mods is listed too when they are installed.
- Good to know: The price follows how well a piece protects you. Within one Age, strong pieces cost more and weak ones less. A piece far stronger than the rest of its Age also needs a rare part, and the list says how strong it is.


# Age Armor Sets
- What it is: Five armor sets made at the Armor Platform, one for each Age: Ranger (Frontier), Trench (World Wars), Operator (Modern), Vanguard Exo (Advanced) and Resonance (Exotic).
- You get: Ranger protects like iron armor and Trench a little more. Operator, Vanguard Exo and Resonance protect like diamond armor. Each set also gives a bonus while you wear all four of its pieces.
- How it works: Make the pieces at the Armor Platform like any other gear and put them on. A piece's tooltip shows its set bonus and how many pieces of the set you wear.
- How to unlock: A set is listed once your Armor Platform reaches its Age.
- Careful: The bonus needs all four pieces of the same set. Mixed sets give armor only.

# Set bonuses
- Quick Draw (Ranger): guns reload 15%% faster.
- Stormtrooper (Trench): guns deal 10%% more damage, and Poison cannot touch you.
- Night Operator (Operator): Night Vision while you wear it, and guns deal 10%% more damage.
- Exo Bulwark (Vanguard Exo): no knockback, 25%% less damage from bullets and explosions, and Slowness cannot touch you.
- Ardent Ward (Resonance): Regeneration, 2 extra hearts and no knockback. When a hit leaves you below 30%% health, a pulse throws nearby enemies back and gives you 4 extra hearts for 10 seconds. It works once a minute.

# Workshop Fabrication
- What it is: A tab on the beacon that sells the starter version of every table and workstation.
- You get: The four tables, the kitchen blocks (Mess Hall, Cook Pot, Bowl Dispenser, Milk Dispenser), the Support Platform, the Support Cannon and the Exchange Shop. Eleven in all.
- How it works: Stand near your planted beacon, open the tab, find the card and press Make. The price comes out of your pack.
- How to unlock: Plant the beacon.
- Careful: Kitchen blocks, the Exchange Shop and support gear must be placed inside your zone.

# Ammo Coins
- What it is: A special coin you only win from raids.
- You get: Ammo without the materials. At the Ammo Platform, Buy with coins pays for the whole batch shown.
- How it works: Win coins, then spend them at the Ammo Platform.
- How to unlock: Complete raids. Coins cannot be crafted.
- Careful: The coin price grows with the Age and the strength of the gun.

# Supplies
- What it is: A category in the Weapon Platform: food, medical kits, grenades, tools and gear materials.
- You get: Everything that is not a gun, ammo or armor.
- How it works: Open the Weapon Platform and pick Supplies.
- How to unlock: Supplies follow your Create research. Simple field gear starts open. Medical kits and grenades need Workshop research, and advanced supplies need Precision research.

# Ages
- What it is: Five levels each table can reach: Frontier, World Wars, Modern, Advanced and Exotic.
- You get: Newer guns, ammo, attachments and gear.
- How it works: Each of the four tables has its own Age. Open a table, pick the Upgrade tab and press the one big Upgrade button. A ladder shows where you are and what comes next, and the materials show what you hold.
- How to unlock: Every table starts at Frontier.
- Careful: Modern and later Ages need a team visit to the Nether and the Create precision parts.
- Careful: Age locks still apply in Survival. A modern pistol stays a Modern unlock.

# Factory parts
- What it is: Receivers, Hardened Alloy, Cartridge Cases and Factory Propellant: the parts your Create factory makes for guns and ammo.
- You get: The materials the weapon tables ask for. Guns need a receiver for their era, and ammo needs cases and propellant.
- How it works: A Mechanical Press makes Pressed Receivers from iron sheets and Cartridge Cases from copper sheets.
- How to unlock: Build the Create machines. Nothing else is needed.
- Careful: Hostile mobs are tougher than usual from the start. The first time anyone holds a better receiver, they get tougher again everywhere. This never goes back.
- Good to know: A Mechanical Mixer makes Factory Propellant, and Hardened Alloy over a heated basin. Brass and Hardened Receivers come off a sequenced assembly line. Exotic Receivers come from Mechanical Crafters. Look them up with {jei}
gui.eternal_defense.guide.stations.detai:
- Benches are two blocks wide and two tall, one deep, and turn to face you. Either half opens the same menu. Mining either half returns one station and keeps its Age; raid repairs do too.
- The Ammo table lists reusable EMPTY magazines as well as loose rounds. Use the filter to switch between loose ammunition and compatible magazines. Craft an empty magazine, then fill it with the magazine addon and your loose rounds. Coins can buy empty magazines but never include free rounds.
- A gun's standard magazine is listed as soon as its rounds are. Expanded magazines need a matching extension on your gun and a later Age. The browser counts items still locked behind later Ages.
- Use the coloured Age filter for weapon eras. Historical identity matters: a modern pistol stays a Modern unlock. Gauss and cyberpunk weapons are Exotic.
- Compatibility and Age locks still apply in Survival. Coin cost scales with Age and the strongest compatible gun damage, including pellets and explosives.
- Fuel weapons that need a Field Radio (Apocalypse bf1:ef46 and bf1:wex) are left out of Universal Weapon Platform crafting.
- Create Armory, Turrets and Supplies have separate category buttons. Supplies follow shared Create research instead of Ages: simple field gear starts unlocked, medical kits and grenades need Workshop research, advanced supplies need Precision research.
- Operate a press and mixer for Workshop, a deployer and a precision mechanism for Precision, and a steam engine for heavy Steam weapons. Turrets need Precision production and factory materials.
- Near-future MS-Mobius weapons need later factory Ages; Helldivers weapons require Exotic. Shared milestones also unlock matching Create Armory components.
gui.eternal_defense.guide.energy.body:
# Ardent Energy
- What it is: A glowing item you win by fighting. It is the money of your base.
- You get: It pays for flares, the Support Cannon and Exchange Shop goods.
- How it works: Mobs with a red "!" (raid and Tactical Operation mobs) drop it now and then, about one kill in ten (more with raid modifiers). Elite mobs always drop it. Every won raid pays a fixed amount, more at higher raid levels.
- How to unlock: Nothing to unlock. Go and fight. You cannot craft it.
- Careful: Ordinary wild mobs drop none. Only big bosses with 300 health or more drop one outside a raid.

# Exchange Shop
- What it is: A shop booth with two tabs, Sell and Buy.
- You get: Sell spare materials for Ardent Energy, or buy supplies with it.
- How it works: Hand in goods on Sell. Spend energy on Buy. Buying always costs more than selling the same thing, so you cannot loop it for profit.
- How to unlock: Buy it at Workshop Fabrication, or craft it from copper, iron, glass and redstone. Place it inside your zone.
- Careful: The offers come from a text file that server admins can change, so a server may sell different things.
gui.eternal_defense.guide.energy.detail:
- Mobs with a red "!" drop at 1.5 times the base chance of 6.67%%, +1%% per Looting level. Raid modifiers and special raids add their percent of the base chance (all of them together: twice the base chance), and Luck adds 25%% a level. Both numbers are in config/eternal-defense-common.toml.
- Offers are plain text in config/eternal-defense-exchange.txt, in a [sell] and a [buy] section: 'minecraft:diamond = 6' is one diamond for 6 energy, 'minecraft:arrow x16 = 3' is sixteen arrows. The default lists Create parts, iron and rare vanilla materials.
- The shop reads its file every time it opens, so edits apply without a restart.
gui.eternal_defense.guide.support.body:
# Support Platform
- What it is: Your own landing pad and supply box. Every player builds their own.
- You get: A place where your deliveries land and where your Return Flare brings you home.
- How it works: Fill its supply grid (3 x 3 at first, up to 6 x 6 as it levels up). It stays where you put it.
- How to unlock: Buy it at Workshop Fabrication, or craft it. Place it inside your zone with the block in front of it clear.
- Careful: You can only have one, and only you can open it. It stops working while the beacon is gone.
- Careful: The two blocks in front of it are a no-build "KEEP RETURN ZONE CLEAR" spot. Keep them empty or your Return Flare cannot bring you home. Sand, gravel or a block pushed in there pops out and drops as an item.
- Good to know: Move it for free with the Recovery Shovel. It keeps its level and contents.

# Support Cannon
- What it is: A big gun that belongs to you. Everything you call goes through it.
- You get: Supplies by parachute, a ride home and bombardments on your enemies.
- How it works: It turns toward your flare with a grinding of gears, locks on with a clunk and fires the moment that sound ends. It handles one call at a time. Click it to choose your fire support and buy upgrades.
- How to unlock: Buy it at your Support Platform or at Workshop Fabrication, for Ardent Energy.
- Careful: One per player, and only the owner can use it. Place it anywhere inside the zone, as far from the platform as you like.

# Support Flare
- What it is: A flare that calls in supplies.
- You get: A chest with everything in your supply grid. It parachutes in outdoors, or appears at your feet underground.
- How it works: Fill the grid at your platform. Throw the flare where you want the supplies. The cannon fires, then the chest arrives. Chat counts the seconds.
- How to unlock: Buy flares at your Support Platform, in the Shop tab.
- Careful: The grid is emptied when the chest is sent, so refill it after every call. If something is missing you keep the flare and get a message.

# Return Flare
- What it is: A ticket home.
- You get: A purple portal that takes you to your Support Platform.
- How it works: Throw it. The cannon fires and a portal opens where the flare landed. Step in. Only you can use it, it works from any dimension, and it closes after 30 seconds.
- How to unlock: Buy it at your Support Platform.
- Careful: It needs a free spot in front of your platform. If there is none, the flare is not used up.

# Fire Support Flare
- What it is: A flare that calls a bombardment.
- You get: Shells that land on enemies inside a red box.
- How it works: Throw it at enemies. The cannon shells the box with the fire support YOU chose. Hold the flare to see your choice above the hotbar. Throw a second one during a barrage and you see "Barrage in process": it waits its turn.
- How to unlock: Buy it at your Support Platform.
- Careful: The Bunker Buster hurts every player inside its box for half their maximum health, whatever armor they wear. If its box touches your beacon zone, the flare is handed back.
- Good to know: Far from your cannon? Chat says "Cannon preparing" when it starts to turn and "You heard cannon fire roaring" when it shoots.
- Good to know: The cannon fires up into the sky. Listen for the scream: about 5 seconds later the shell drops straight onto the flare.


# Handheld Radio
- What it is: A field radio that carries your flares.
- You get: Flare calls without throwing. The chosen flare is planted right where you look, up to 48 blocks away.
- How it works: Sneak and use it to open its menu. Put Support, Return, Fire Support and Loadout Flares in their slots, up to 16 of each. Pick the flare to plant and the kit a Loadout Flare brings. Then look at the ground and use the radio.
- How to unlock: Buy it at your Support Platform.
- Careful: Each call uses one flare from the radio. If the call is refused, nothing is used.
- Good to know: Picking a kit in the radio also changes the active kit at your Loadout Station.

# Fire support types
- Explosion Barrage: shells that explode on the target.
- Spotter Arrows: a small hit on every hostile mob in the box, which then glows and takes 30%% more damage from everything until it dies.
- Narukami's Favor: lightning on every hostile mob, with 1 fewer volley.
- Bunker Buster: one huge bomb that digs out everything in its box and hits as hard as five shells.
- Healing Barrage: heals players inside.
- Curse of Debilitation: puts the worst debuffs on hostile mobs, until they die.
- Cluster Strike: one shell, then bomblets rain on a wide area for 12 seconds.
- Cryo Shell: snow on the ground; hostile mobs in it nearly stop. No damage.
- Napalm Carpet: the ground burns; mobs caught in it are set Ablaze and burn until they die, even in water.
- Gravity Well: a wide vortex drags hostile mobs into one crowd to shoot. No damage.
- Shockwave: shoves every hostile mob in a huge area out to its edge. No damage.
- Starshell: lights up a huge area for 30 seconds, up to a minute with More volley. Hostile mobs glow, you move faster.

# Cannon upgrades
- What it is: Ten upgrades you buy by clicking your cannon.
- You get: Faster turning, faster fire, more shells, more damage, a wider area, reach underground, a longer-lasting portal, a healing aura, a slowing field and fire support in other dimensions.
- How it works: Click your cannon, open the upgrades and buy with factory parts. The Reference tab lists the prices.
- How to unlock: Buy the cannon first.
- Careful: Without Quantum tunneling, a fire support or Loadout flare under 3 or more solid blocks (a cave, a tunnel) is handed back. An open pit is fine. Without Dimensional link it does not work in other dimensions.
gui.eternal_defense.guide.support.detail:
- Prices at the platform: Support Flare 3 energy, Return Flare 2, Fire Support Flare 6, Loadout Flare 5, Handheld Radio 8, Support Cannon 12. The Exchange Shop and the Support Platform are also sold in the beacon’s Workshop Fabrication tab for iron, copper, redstone and glass.
- Supplies arrive 12 seconds after the cannon fires for a flare that landed outdoors, or 7 seconds underground. Chat counts the seconds down. The time the cannon spends turning comes on top.
- The cannon is heavy: it spins up and brakes slowly, so a flare behind it takes longer to answer (a half turn takes about 7 seconds, and about 5 with Faster traverse at its top level). Once it is on target it locks on and fires 0.9 seconds later. It can only work on one call at a time.
- Fire Support lasts 12 seconds (6 shells). Each shell takes 5 seconds from the shot to the impact. Each shell deals 25 damage to hostile mobs touching the red box (within 4 blocks of the flare) and never hurts players or breaks blocks.
- The Bunker Buster is the exception: its box reaches 8 blocks down as well as up and sideways, every block inside it is dug out (the Defense Beacon, base blocks and super hard blocks such as obsidian, crying obsidian and bedrock are spared), and it hurts every player inside for half their maximum health, whatever armor they wear. If its box touches your beacon zone the flare is handed back.
- The Bunker Buster's blow deals 125 damage to every hostile mob in its box, as much as five barrage shells, and more with each Damage level.
- The portal stays open for 30 seconds and only its owner can use it. It works from any dimension.
- When the cannon takes a flare’s call, your radio answers. Fire support, supply and return flares each have their own lines.
- Parcels disappear after 30 minutes and drop what is left inside.
- Upgrades Mk-2, Mk-3 and Mk-4 cost 16, 32 and 64 reinforced plating and grow the grid to 4 x 4, 5 x 5 and 6 x 6.
- Only the owner can open their platform or cannon.
- Each Area of effect level widens the area by 1.5 blocks each way.
- Cluster Strike: one shell bursts 6 blocks up over an area 1.75 times as wide, then bomblets go off there for 12 seconds. Every half second each hostile mob inside takes 6.25 damage: 150 in all, as much as six barrage shells.
- Cryo Shell: one shell; snow covers the ground 7.8 blocks each way from the flare (3 blocks more each way than the napalm), 2 blocks high, for 15 seconds (+5 per More volley level). Hostile mobs in it get Slowness V (a raid boss Slowness III). No damage.
- Napalm Carpet: one shell; real fire covers an area 1.2 times as wide, 2 blocks high, for 10 seconds (+4 per More volley level). Mobs inside take 5 damage a second and burn. No fire is lit within 4 blocks of the beacon zone.
- Ablaze: each hostile mob that can burn and stands in the burning napalm is set Ablaze until it dies. It takes 4 damage a second (more with the Damage upgrade, half for a raid boss), even in water or rain. Blazes and other fire-proof mobs are not affected.
- Spotter Arrows: 6 volleys; each hits every hostile mob in the box for 4 damage, with no knockback, and marks it until it dies. A marked mob glows and takes 30%% more from every hit, guns included (a raid boss 15%%). Marks do not stack.
- Curse of Debilitation: every hostile mob one shell touches keeps Wither II, Poison II, Weakness II, Slowness III and Blindness until it dies. The Damage upgrade does not change it.
- Gravity Well: one shell; for 6 seconds (+2 per More volley level, 12 at the top level) hostile mobs in an area twice as wide are dragged to the flare. No damage. A raid boss is barely moved.
- Shockwave: 4 shells; each shoves every hostile mob within 8 blocks of the flare out past the edge, bosses too. No damage.
- Starshell: one star that burns 30 seconds (+10 per More volley level, a full minute at the top level) and lights everything within 16 blocks. Hostile mobs there glow and players there get Speed II, which lasts 30 seconds after they leave the light. Each Area of effect level adds 2 blocks.
- Each volley level adds 2 shells and each damage level adds 25 percent. Rate of fire cuts the gap between shells from 40 ticks to 33, 26 and 20.
- Without Quantum tunneling a fire support or Loadout flare with 3 or more solid blocks above it is handed back (leaves and thin roofs do not count). Supply and return flares are not affected.
- Dimensional link lets fire support and Loadout flares work in the Nether, the End and other dimensions (the cannon still needs your base to stand). Supply and return flares are not affected.
- The Lasting portal stays open for 5 minutes and works twice: once home, once back to where you threw it.
- The Healing aura circles a supply flare (6 blocks) and ends 30 seconds after the parcel is emptied.
- Cannon upgrades are paid in the mod's factory parts, never in Ardent Energy. Reinforced plating: Faster traverse 6, 12 and 24, Area of effect 5, 10 and 20. Resonance coils: Rate of fire 5, 10 and 20, Damage 6, 12 and 24, Slowness field 10. Logistics modules: More volley 6, 12 and 24, Lasting portal 10. Restoration matrices: Quantum tunneling 6, Healing aura 4, Dimensional link 10. The Exchange Shop sells parts for Ardent Energy.
gui.eternal_defense.guide.reference.body: ~ The small print: exact numbers and extra rules from every other page, in one place. You do not need it to play.
gui.eternal_defense.guide.coop.body:
# Playing together
- What it is: Everyone on the server plays one shared campaign.
- You get: One team, one base and one set of prizes.
- How it works: You share the beacon, its upgrades, the raid level cap and the reward chest. Your Support Platform, Support Cannon, flare choice and meals are yours alone.
- How to unlock: Nothing needed. Just join.
- Careful: Anyone with a Recovery Shovel can reset the campaign for everybody. The game asks first, but talk to your team.
- Good to know: The red BEACON IS BEING ATTACKED warning reaches every player, without holding a tool.

# Pack co-op
- Everyone needs the same pack version. Play on a server, or open your world to LAN.

gui.eternal_defense.guide.kitchen.title: Mess Hall & meals
gui.eternal_defense.guide.kitchen.body:
# Mess Hall
- What it is: Your kitchen counter. You put food on it and it cooks meals that boost you.
- You get: Sandwiches you carry with you, and big pots of stew for the whole team.
- How it works: Open it. Buttons that do things are on the left; the effects you can choose are on the right. Click the effects you want, press Gather ingredients and the hall lays out the right food from your pack and your Logistics Hubs, then press Make sandwich or Cook stew.
- How to unlock: Craft one from planks, a furnace, iron and a barrel, or buy it at Workshop Fabrication. Place it inside your zone.
- Careful: Gather ingredients spends nothing. Cooking does. Take back puts the table's food in your pack, not back in a Hub. Choose no recipes and the hall picks effects from whatever food you put on the table.

# Sandwich
- What it is: A meal you carry in your pack.
- You get: One or two effects, usable anywhere. They stack up to 16.
- How it works: Put two bread in the Base slot and two or three different foods in the other slots, then press Make sandwich. Each food is used two at a time.
- How to unlock: Every Mess Hall makes them, even a Mk I.
- Careful: The bread in the Base slot never gives an effect. Only the fillings do.

# Cook Pot and stew
- What it is: A pot that holds a big batch of stew for many people.
- You get: Up to three effects and 5 to 9 servings, depending on your hall's level.
- How it works: Put the pot within 8 blocks of the hall and pick it on the hall screen, then press Cook stew. Right-click the full pot with a bowl to eat. The bowl is used up. A board on the pot shows the effects and the servings left.
- How to unlock: Your Mess Hall must be Mk II or better. Craft the pot from iron, a sign and a cauldron, or buy it at Workshop Fabrication.
- Careful: A Mk I hall cannot cook stew. Cooking into a pot that still has stew asks you first, and the old stew is thrown away. A cook that cannot work spends nothing.

# What a meal does
- What it is: Food buffs. They show as ordinary potion effects, plus a "Home Zone" effect.
- You get: More health, armor, damage and luck, slower hunger and less damage from blasts and arrows, plus gun boosts like faster reload and less recoil.
- How it works: A meal lasts 15, 20, 25 or 30 minutes in the field, longer from a higher level hall. At home, inside your zone, every value is DOUBLE and the timer stops. Logging out pauses it too.
- How to unlock: Just eat one.
- Careful: Dying clears your meal. Milk clears it too. A new meal replaces the old one.

# Hardy, Blast Ward and Projectile Ward
- What it is: Three everyday meal effects that help you last in a fight.
- You get: Hardy makes you hungry 15%% slower. Blast Ward takes 20%% off explosion damage. Projectile Ward takes 15%% off arrows, crossbow bolts, fireballs and tridents.
- How it works: Choose them in the Mess Hall like any everyday effect. Fish and sweets feed Hardy, rotten flesh and spider eyes feed Blast Ward, chorus fruit and melon feed Projectile Ward.
- How to unlock: Every Mess Hall can make them, even a Mk I.
- Careful: At home every value doubles, but Hardy stops at 60%%, Blast Ward at 80%% and Projectile Ward at 90%%. Blast Ward does not stop fire. Projectile Ward does not stop gun bullets.

# Mess Hall levels
- What it is: Four levels of hall, Mk I to Mk IV. Each one adds something.
- You get: Mk I: sandwiches only. Meals last 15 minutes. 3 food slots.
- Mk II: unlocks stew. Meals last 20 minutes.
- Mk III: meals last 25 minutes. Unlocks ×2 doubling (see below).
- Mk IV: meals last 30 minutes. Opens all 6 food slots.
- How it works: Open the hall and press Upgrade to Mk N on the left. It lights up when you can afford it. Hover it to see what the next level gives.
- How to unlock: Pay 8, 16 and 32 Reinforced Beacon Plating.
- Careful: Your food and pot links stay when you upgrade. Creative mode is free.

# Doubling (×2)
- What it is: A way to make one effect count twice.
- You get: That effect is twice as strong. Its card in your order shows ×2.
- How it works: Put two DIFFERENT foods of the same type on the table that both give the effect, for example cooked chicken and cooked mutton for Vitality. One food is not enough, and two stacks of the same food do not count. Gather does it for you when your pack allows.
- How to unlock: Upgrade the hall to Mk III.
- Careful: A legendary effect needs two different foods from EACH of its two groups. That is four food slots, so only a Mk IV hall can double one.

# Bowl Dispenser
- What it is: A box of bowls for eating stew.
- You get: A bowl with one right-click. A message tells you how many are left.
- How it works: To stock it, crouch with BOTH hands empty and right-click. Put up to 64 bowls inside. Every serving eaten from a Cook Pot uses up a bowl, so keep it stocked.
- How to unlock: Buy it at Workshop Fabrication.
- Careful: It cannot make bowls. When it is empty it only tells you so. Breaking it drops its bowls.

# Milk Dispenser and Milk Bottle
- What it is: A tank of milk that cleans you.
- You get: Right-click and every effect on you is cleared.
- How it works: Each use takes 250 mB from an 8,000 mB tank. Refill it with milk buckets (1,000 mB) or Milk Bottles (250 mB): crouch with empty hands and right-click to open it. A message tells you what it cleared.
- How to unlock: Buy the dispenser at Workshop Fabrication. Craft 4 Milk Bottles from a milk bucket and 4 glass bottles (you keep the bucket).
- Careful: It clears EVERYTHING, good effects and your meal too. If you have nothing to clear it says so and spends nothing.
gui.eternal_defense.guide.kitchen.detail:
- Everyday effects need any food that feeds them. A legendary effect needs one food from EACH of two groups and replaces the everyday bonuses of those groups. Two chosen legendary recipes cannot share a group.
- Doubling unlocks at Mk III, in sandwiches and in stew: two different foods of one group for an everyday effect. A legendary effect needs two different foods from EACH group, which takes four food slots, so only Mk IV can double one. Split stacks never count twice. Gather doubles whenever your pack allows it.
- Gather uses what is already on the table first, then your pack, and never spends anything. Take back returns the whole table.
- Your order and mode stay with the hall. Close the screen and come back to find it as you left it.
- Mk I to IV: meals last 15/20/25/30 field minutes. Food slots 3/3/3/6. Stew from Mk II, doubling from Mk III. Stew uses 1/2/3/4 linked pots, 3/5/7/9 servings and 12/21/30/36 food units per cook. A sandwich uses 2 bread and 2 of each filling. Pots link within 8 blocks.
- A meal lasts as long as its hall allows (15 to 30 field minutes). At home every value doubles and the timer freezes. Logout pauses it; death and milk clear it; a new meal replaces the old one.
- Bowl Dispenser: right-click for a bowl. Crouch with both hands empty to open it and stock one stack of bowls.
- Milk Dispenser: right-click spends 250 mB and clears every effect, including your meal. With nothing to clear it spends nothing. Buckets (1,000 mB) and Milk Bottles (250 mB) refill it; empties come out of the output slot.
- Milk Bottle: one milk bucket plus four glass bottles craft four bottles and return the bucket. Drinking one clears every effect and returns the glass.

Hall upgrades cost 8/16/32 Reinforced Plating. TaCZ Attributes 1.4 is required on client and server alongside TaCZ 1.1.8-hotfix2.

gui.eternal_defense.guide.mixes.body:
# Legendary meals
- What it is: Special meals that help you handle guns.
- You get: Small bonuses while the meal lasts: damage, reload speed, recoil, accuracy and more.
- How it works: Each one needs foods from TWO specific food groups (list below). In the Mess Hall click its icon in the second row and press Gather ingredients.
- How to unlock: Nothing to unlock. All fifteen are open once you have a Mess Hall and the right foods.
- Careful: A legendary meal uses up BOTH of its food groups, so those groups cannot also feed everyday effects. Two legendary picks cannot share a group.

# The fifteen mixes
- Protein + Grain: Firepower (+8%% gun damage in the field)
- Fruit + Grain: Quick Hands (+10%% reload speed)
- Protein + Fungi: Brawler (+20%% gun bash damage)
- Protein + Vegetables: Heavy Hand (+15%% gun bash knockback)
- Fish + Fungi: Demolition (+10%% grenade and rocket radius)
- Vegetables + Grain: Recoil Control (−10%% recoil)
- Fish + Vegetables: Focus (+10%% aimed and hip-fire accuracy)
- Fish + Fruit: Snap Aim (+10%% aiming speed)
- Fruit + Fungi: Fast Draw (+10%% draw speed)
- Protein + Fish: Dead Eye (+8%% headshot damage)
- Protein + Fruit: Gun Mobility (+8%% gun movement-speed multiplier)
- Fish + Grain: Impact (+0.25 bullet knockback)
- Vegetables + Fruit: Rapid Fire (+5%% rate of fire)
- Vegetables + Fungi: Scoped Focus (+15%% aimed accuracy)
- Grain + Fungi: Hip Focus (+15%% hip-fire accuracy)
~ A Mk IV hall can double a legendary effect: two different foods from each of its groups (four food slots). At home every value doubles again. Six different groups, which needs all six food slots, make three legendary effects at once.
gui.eternal_defense.guide.mixes.detail:
# Everyday ×2 pairs (Mk III and up)
- Vitality: cooked chicken + cooked mutton.
- Fortitude: carrot + potato.
- Steadiness: brown mushroom + red mushroom (bread + wheat also works).
- Hardy: cooked cod + cooked salmon.
- Might: raw beef + cooked beef.
- Agility: cookie + pumpkin pie.
- Fortune: apple + glow berries.
- Recovery: honey bottle + golden apple.
- Blast Ward: rotten flesh + spider eye.
- Projectile Ward: chorus fruit + melon slice.
- Swim: raw cod + raw salmon.
~ Apple also feeds Fortune and melon also feeds Projectile Ward. Hover any recipe icon to see every food that feeds it.
# Food groups
- Protein & dairy: raw and cooked land meat, egg, milk, rabbit stew.
- Fish: raw and cooked fish, pufferfish.
- Vegetables: carrot, potato, beetroot, beetroot soup, dried kelp, golden carrot.
- Fruit & sweets: apples, berries, melon, sugar, honey, golden apples, chorus.
- Grain: bread, wheat, baked potato, cookie, pumpkin pie.
- Fungi & fermented: mushrooms, mushroom and suspicious stew, rotten flesh, spider eye, poisonous potato.
~ Each food belongs to one group and each distinct item counts once. A legendary recipe reserves BOTH its groups; other groups can still feed everyday effects you choose.

# Gun Guide
- What it is: A small card on your screen that lists the controls of the gun in your hand. It is its own mod and only runs on your computer.
- You get: Your real keys for Fire, Aim, Reload, Fire mode, Melee, Inspect, Attachments and more. A warning if two actions share one key. A red JAM alert when your gun jams.
- How it works: Draw a gun and the card opens for five seconds, then shrinks to a small badge. Press its key to open or hide it. Change the key in Controls, under Eternal Defense Gun Guide.
- How to unlock: Install the Gun Guide mod. There is nothing to craft.
- Careful: The JAM alert only works with the TaCZ Durability addon. Without it the controls card still works.

# Gun Displays
- What it is: Eleven decoration blocks for showing off guns: stands, wall racks and glass cases. Some are wide, some are made for pistols and one is for heavy weapons.
- You get: A trophy room for your best guns.
- How it works: Hold a gun, look at a stand and press {interact} to put it on display. Press {interact} with another gun to swap them. Right-click with empty hands to take it back.
- How to unlock: Install the Gun Displays mod. Every stand has its own crafting table recipe; JEI shows them. You can also buy them in the Weapon Platform's Supplies category.
- Careful: Wall racks need a solid wall behind every part. Glass cases show guns smaller so magazines clear the glass.
- Good to know: A Weapon Display Tuner, made from an iron nugget, an iron ingot and a stick, changes how a gun sits on its stand. Right-click a stand with it to change the gun's size, position and angle. The settings stay with the stand when you swap guns.

gui.eternal_defense.guide.tactical.title: Tactical Ops
gui.eternal_defense.guide.tactical.body:
# Command Table
- What it is: A war table for your base. It shows a satellite map around your beacon and the missions your satellite finds.
- You get: Hunting missions for the whole team. Wipe out a warband out in the wild and the pay lands in the beacon's reward chest.
- How it works: Click it. Pick an X on the map or an offer in the list, then press Accept. Everyone online gets a map with your base and a red X on it, and one Return Flare.
- How to unlock: Buy it at Workshop Fabrication. Place it inside your zone. It is 2 blocks wide, 2 deep and 2 tall.
- Careful: One per base. It needs a Satellite Beacon within 8 blocks that can see the sky. Without one it shows NO UPLINK and you cannot accept anything.
- Careful: You cannot accept a mission during a raid or in the last day before one (RAID WARNING). A mission that is already running goes on.
- Good to know: Press SCAN MAP to refresh the map. Only land near a player shows live. The rest keeps its last scan (dimmed) or its land type (hatched).
- Good to know: Lost your map? Press Reprint map at the table. Move the table for free with the Recovery Shovel.
- Good to know: The FOBs tab lists every FOB with its distance from the base. A FOB calling for help shows its SOS time left, and Reprint SOS map gives you a new copy of the SOS map.
- Good to know: The map shows your FOBs and their village zones. A FOB beyond the map's edge gets an arrow with its name, pointing its way.

# Satellite Beacon
- What it is: A dish that finds enemy warbands for the Command Table.
- You get: Offers on the board: 2 at Mk I, 3 at Mk II and 4 at Mk III. Its reach grows from 256 to 512 and then 1024 blocks.
- How it works: Place it within 8 blocks of the table where it sees the sky. Click it to check the link. Upgrade it with the button at the top of the table's screen.
- How to unlock: Buy it at Workshop Fabrication. Upgrades cost resonance coils: 16 for Mk II and 32 for Mk III.
- Careful: One per base. Mk II also finds Garrisons and Mk III also finds Warlords.
- Good to know: Move it for free with the Recovery Shovel. It keeps its Mk.

# Hunting missions
- What it is: A warband out in the wild that your team hunts down together. One mission runs at a time.
- You get: Ardent Energy and ammo coins in the beacon's reward chest, paid once when the last enemy falls. Higher reward tiers pay more.
- How it works: Accept an offer. Follow your map to the red X. When someone gets within 64 blocks, a small zone lights up on solid ground at the X and the warband comes out of red gates around it, then rushes in. Kill every one: the status card counts them down.
- How to unlock: Place a Command Table and a Satellite Beacon. The board fills as soon as they link.
- Careful: If everybody stays more than 128 blocks away from a warband for 5 minutes, it scatters. Nothing is paid for it. Go back to the red X for a new one.
- Careful: Abandon sends the warband away and puts the offer back on the board. Nobody gets a second Return Flare for that offer.
- Good to know: Each extra player online adds 2 enemies, up to 8 more. Hunt enemies carry the raid's red mark and drop no Ardent Energy themselves: the pay is in the chest.
- Good to know: The mission line on your status card shows while you hold the mission map or the Recovery Shovel. When the operation is over, its maps burn.
- Careful: No ground at all near the X, such as open water? A return gate opens in front of you for 5 minutes and a new offer replaces that one.
- Good to know: A finished offer is replaced at the next dawn, one new offer a day. Taking the beacon down ends the running mission.

# Mission types
- Colours on the table: Patrol blue, Garrison purple, Warlord gold. The X you have picked turns red.
- Patrol: 8 to 12 enemies on open ground. It pays a little less than a Garrison.
- Garrison: 14 to 20 enemies camped around a structure, such as a pillager outpost or a desert temple. Its loot stays where it is. Needs Mk II. With no such structure in range, a Patrol is offered instead.
- Warlord: a glowing captain with twice the health, named after the operation, and 10 to 14 escorts. The biggest pay. Needs Mk III.

# Warlord Seal
- What it is: A war trophy taken from a Warlord, the hardest hunt.
- You get: One treasure enchant unlocked for the whole team at the Tactical Enchanting Table.
- How it works: Clear a Warlord hunt and the seal lands in the beacon's reward chest. At the table, click Unlock beside a treasure enchant.
- How to unlock: Your Satellite Beacon finds Warlords from Mk III.
- Careful: Soul Speed and Swift Sneak take one more seal for level II and one more for level III.
- Good to know: A seal you do not need sells at the Exchange Shop for Ardent Energy.
gui.eternal_defense.guide.tactical.detai:
- Command Table at Workshop Fabrication: 24 iron, 16 copper, 16 redstone, 8 glass and 4 reinforced plating. Satellite Beacon: 16 iron, 24 copper, 8 redstone, 4 gold and 2 resonance coils.
- Pay at reward tier 3: Patrol 2 Ardent Energy and 8 ammo coins, Garrison 2 and 9, Warlord 4 and 15. Pay grows with the Next payout tier shown on your beacon, up to tier 10, and each offer card shows its own. Every mission pays at least 1 Ardent Energy and 2 ammo coins, a Patrol at least 2 and 4.
- Objectives lie at least 150 blocks beyond the edge of your zone, never in the same direction as another offer, and never on an ocean or a river.
- The warband needs one block to stand on within 16 blocks of the X. Its zone is 6 blocks wide each way; enemies come out 8 to 12 blocks from the middle and stay within 32 blocks of it.
- Enemies never burn in daylight and never attack the beacon.
- SCAN MAP can be pressed again 30 seconds after a scan ends. One scan runs at a time for the whole server.
- A Warlord Seal sells for 4 Ardent Energy at the Exchange Shop.
gui.eternal_defense.guide.fob.title: FOBs
gui.eternal_defense.guide.fob.body:
# FOB Beacon
- What it is: A flag post you plant in a village. It turns the village into a Forward Operating Base (FOB), an outpost of your base.
- You get: A FOB shop that sells Support, Return and Fire Support Flares far from home. Your meal buffs double and stop running down in its village. Its villagers cannot be hurt.
- How it works: Plant it in a village with at least 3 villagers. A raid on the village starts at once. Win it and the FOB turns ACTIVE. Click the FOB Beacon to see the village, the raid and the shop.
- How it works: Hold the FOB Beacon and look at the ground. A see-through FOB shows where it would stand, an outline shows the part of the village it would take, and a line under the crosshair counts its villagers, beds and workstations. Green means you can plant it there.
- How to unlock: Buy it at Workshop Fabrication. Plant your Defense Beacon first.
- Careful: A red FOB means something is in the way, like a block above it. Move until it is not red.
- Careful: The FOB goes DOWN if fewer than half of the villagers living there when the raid began are still alive, or if the village falls. A DOWN FOB sells and sends nothing until you repair it at its FOB Beacon.
- Careful: Now and then an ACTIVE FOB calls for help (an SOS). Go to its village in time: its raid starts when you arrive. Lose it, or stay away, and the FOB goes DOWN.
- Careful: While its raid runs, its villagers can be hurt, by you too.
- Careful: Only the Recovery Shovel takes a FOB Beacon back, after a confirmation. That deletes the FOB.
- Good to know: The flares work as they do at home. Every flare needs your Support Platform and your Support Cannon.
- Good to know: Up to 5 FOBs, one per village, in the Overworld. All players share them.
- Good to know: Use a Name Tag renamed at an anvil on the FOB Beacon to rename the FOB.
- Good to know: An olive outline shows each FOB's zone when you are near it. Step inside for the meal bonus and the shop. Turn it off with Zone outline on the FOB's screen.
- Good to know: Raiders of village raids drop no Ardent Energy. Raiders of your beacon raids still do.
- Good to know: Villagers killed in a FOB's raid are not gone for good. The repair at the FOB Beacon brings them back, with their trades.

# Supply Delivery Gate
- What it is: The FOB end of a supply route: a gate 4 blocks wide and 2 tall that stands across two rail lanes in the FOB's village.
- You get: The FOB's tribute (emeralds, plus the mine, farm and specialty items you choose) sent home to the Receiving Gate's storage.
- How it works: Use it on a straight rail in the village. Lay two rails side by side and it stands across both; on a lone rail the other lane stays empty. It links to that FOB by itself, and both gates show the FOB's name.
- How to unlock: Buy it at Workshop Fabrication, or at the FOB shop while the FOB is ACTIVE. One per FOB.
- Careful: It cannot be mined. Move it with the Recovery Shovel. A moved gate needs a new opening ride.

# Supply Receiving Gate
- What it is: The home end of a supply route: a gate 4 blocks wide and 2 tall that stands across two rail lanes in your base zone.
- You get: The place where every ride starts and ends, and the storage where the FOB's tribute lands.
- How it works: Use it on a straight rail in your zone, then pick the FOB it serves on its screen. Like the Delivery Gate it takes two rails side by side, or one. Its screen shows the storage on the left (on a small window, on its Storage tab): take what you need.
- How to unlock: Buy it at Workshop Fabrication. One per FOB, so up to 5.
- Careful: The two gates must stand at least 128 blocks apart.
- Careful: The storage is take only, a double chest's worth. When it is full, deliveries wait.

# Supply route
- What it is: The line between a FOB's two gates. A traffic light on each gate says how it is doing.
- You get: Tribute in the Receiving Gate's storage by itself, and more when you ride it yourself.
- How it works: Sit in a minecart and ride from the Supply Receiving Gate to the Supply Delivery Gate once to open the route. After that it delivers by itself, and the rail may go. Ride a full round trip (home, FOB, home) to bring up to two deliveries at once.
- How it works: Pick the tribute on the Tribute tab of either gate. Every village sends emeralds. The mine, the farm and the village's specialty each send the one item you choose.
- How it works: Switch a slot off and the slots still on share its part of every delivery. Switch three off and the last one gets it all.
- How to unlock: An ACTIVE FOB with both of its gates placed.
- Careful: Every round trip renews the inspection for 8 hours of play. When it runs out the light turns red and deliveries stop until someone rides again.
- Careful: Deliveries wait while the Receiving Gate's storage is full. Take things out.
- Careful: The specialty (fishing and animal husbandry, potion makers, a wandering trader hub or a monster hunter guild) is picked when the FOB is planted. To get another, take the FOB Beacon back with the shovel and win a new FOB. Its research starts again from zero.
- Good to know: Green means running. Amber means a ride is under way, the inspection ends soon, or the storage is full. Red means something is missing, and the gate's screen says what.
- Good to know: Rare items take more deliveries each. The gate's screen says how many, and the time to the next delivery.
- Good to know: A faster rail pays: the route delivers by itself as often as your ride was fast.
- Good to know: Far routes pay a bonus, up to 20 percent more from 5,000 blocks between the gates.
- Good to know: Best build: two rails side by side through both gates, joined by a curve at each end. The cart goes out on one rail and comes home on the other without stopping.
- Good to know: Even the smallest FOB, with its S tier open, sends an S-tier item every 30 minutes of play.

# Village research
- What it is: A bar on each FOB Beacon's Research tab. Every FOB has its own.
- You get: Its rare specialty items (the A tier at level 2, the S tier at level 4) and bigger deliveries: each level adds 25 percent to the specialty and 5 percent to emeralds, the mine and the farm. Level 5 opens the Supply Catapult and the Specialty Shop.
- How it works: Open the FOB Beacon, click Research and give emeralds, diamonds or Ardent Energy with +1 or +10. A diamond counts 4, an Ardent Energy 2, an emerald 1.
- How to unlock: An ACTIVE FOB. Locked items show a padlock in the gate's Choose list.
- Careful: The research belongs to the FOB. Taking the FOB Beacon back with the shovel throws it away.
- Careful: A specialty sends at most 4 S-tier items' worth an hour, however big the FOB and however many slots you switch off.
- Good to know: Monster hunter guild: every monster drop except the bosses'. Ender pearls and blaze rods are its A tier, so a FOB can feed your eyes of ender.

# Supply Catapult
- What it is: A wooden throwing machine you place in a FOB's village. It sends you that FOB's specialty items, bought for Ardent Energy.
- You get: Any item of the FOB's specialty, whenever you want it, without waiting for deliveries.
- How it works: At the Command Table, open the FOBs tab and click Contact Specialty Seller. Pick an item and buy a lot. The seller shows the catapult live: it turns toward your Defense Beacon and throws the box. Your chat counts down 12 seconds, then the box parachutes down beside the beacon.
- How to unlock: Buy it at Workshop Fabrication and place it in the village, one per FOB. The seller opens when that FOB's research reaches level 5 and the FOB is ACTIVE.
- Careful: It holds 4 boxes at a time. The box needs open sky beside the beacon to parachute in. Otherwise it appears there.
- Good to know: A lot is worth one S-tier item: 1 ghast tear, 2 ender pearls, a stack of cheap items.

# Tactical Enchanting Table
- What it is: A war desk that enchants your gear for Ardent Energy, with no experience, no lapis and no books.
- You get: Any enchant that fits the gear in its slot, level by level. Your ACTIVE FOBs open the higher levels.
- How it works: Click it, put a weapon, a tool or armor in its slot and click a level. A locked level says what it needs.
- How to unlock: Buy it at Workshop Fabrication and place it in your zone. One per base.
- Careful: Level I is always open. The top level of an enchant needs all five FOBs ACTIVE, and a FOB that is DOWN does not count.
- Good to know: Upgrade the table to Mk I, II and III for 17, 33 and 50 percent off every enchant, for everyone.
- Good to know: Treasure enchants (Mending, Frost Walker, Soul Speed, Swift Sneak) open with a Warlord Seal. Curses are never sold.
- Good to know: Vanilla enchanting tables, librarians and anvils work as always.
gui.eternal_defense.guide.fob.detail:
- FOB Beacon at Workshop Fabrication: 16 iron, 16 copper, 8 redstone, 4 glass, 2 logistics modules and 2 reinforced plating.
- FOB shop: Support Flare 3, Return Flare 2 and Fire Support Flare 6 Ardent Energy, the same as at the Support Platform.
- The raid is a village raid started with Bad Omen I: 3 waves on Easy, 5 on Normal and 7 on Hard.
- The FOB goes DOWN when fewer than half of the villagers living there at the start of the raid are alive. With 7 villagers, keep 4.
- The village zone is every 16-block section within one section of a bed, a workstation or a bell that a villager has claimed, joined to the FOB Beacon, up to 6 sections sideways and 3 up or down. Only loaded land counts.
- A FOB name has at most 32 characters. No two FOBs share a name, in any case.
- An SOS comes 10 to 12 hours of play after the last one. It waits while your beacon is raided or a raid is due within a day. You have 7 days of play to answer it.
- Repair: 3 Ardent Energy, plus 1, 1, 2, 2 or 3 for each lost villager from Novice to Master.
- A FOB that never won a raid starts its raid again after the repair.
- Each supply gate: 16 iron, 8 copper, 8 redstone, 2 chests and 1 logistics module.
- A FOB makes tribute by the hour of play. The smallest (3 villagers, gates 128 blocks apart, every slot on) makes 64 an hour.
- Up to 20 villagers make up to twice that, a line up to 1,000 blocks long up to twice again. The far bonus adds the rest.
- The slots that are on share it equally. A delivery brings what was made since the last one, so a faster rail sends it more often.
- A slot's item takes its worth from that share: most items are worth 1, an iron ingot 2, an emerald 4. Tiered items are worth 1, 2, 4, 8 or 16 (D to S).
- A wandering trader's item is worth its emerald price times 16, divided by 6: blue ice, at 6 emeralds, is worth an S-tier item.
- With S open, the smallest FOB's specialty makes 32 an hour: an S-tier item every 30 minutes of play.
- Research: 16, 48, 96, 160 and 240 points for levels 1 to 5. An emerald counts 1, a diamond 4, an Ardent Energy 2.
- Each research level adds 25 percent to the specialty and 5 percent to emeralds, the mine and the farm. Level 2 opens the A tier, level 4 the S tier.
- Potion makers, S tier: ghast tear, rabbit's foot, turtle shell and dragon's breath. A tier: phantom membrane, pufferfish and blaze powder.
- Monster hunter guild, A tier: ender pearl, blaze rod, phantom membrane, nautilus shell. S tier: ghast tear, shulker shell, wither skeleton skull.
- Wandering trader hub, A tier: slime ball, packed ice, the coral blocks and both fish buckets. S tier: nautilus shell and blue ice.
- Emeralds, when on, come at least 1 every 3 deliveries.
- Far bonus: nothing up to 1,000 blocks, then rising to 20 percent more at 5,000 blocks.
- A delivery by itself comes every 2.5 times the one-way ride time, never more often than every 5 minutes of play.
- A round trip you ride brings up to two deliveries: 2.5 times what the route sends by itself in the time since the last delivery. Riding back to back on a fast rail gets the full two.
- The inspection lasts 8 hours of play; the light turns amber in its last 2 hours. Only time with a player online counts.
- Tactical Enchanting Table: 12 iron, 4 obsidian, 3 books and 2 resonance coils. Mk I, II and III: 8, 16 and 32 resonance coils.
- An enchant level costs its rarity's price times the level: 8 for common enchants, 12 for uncommon, 20 for rare and 32 for very rare, in Ardent Energy. Treasure enchants cost twice that. A table at Mk III halves every price.
- ACTIVE FOBs needed for level L of an enchant with M levels: 5 x (L - 1) / (M - 1), rounded up. Sharpness II needs 2, III needs 3, IV needs 4 and V needs 5.
- Supply Catapult at Workshop Fabrication: 16 logs, 8 iron, 16 string and 2 logistics modules. A lot costs 2 Ardent Energy.
