gui.eternal_defense.guide.drinks.title: Drink Station & drinks
gui.eternal_defense.guide.drinks.body:
# Drink Station
- What it is: A brewing counter with its own potion storage. From Mk II it mixes potions into drinks.
- You get: A brewing stand, 54 storage slots that each hold 64 bottles of one potion, and drinks with up to three effects.
- How it works: Open it. Brew on the left as in a brewing stand; finished bottles move into the storage below. On the right, click the effects you want, press Gather potions, then Brew or Make Latte.
- How to unlock: Craft one around a brewing stand, or buy it at Workshop Fabrication. Place it inside your zone.
- Careful: Only drinkable potions with one good effect that lasts can be mixed. Splash, lingering, instant, harmful and Turtle Master potions can only be stored. Regeneration goes in the sweetener.
- Careful: A station holding more than 256 bottles cannot be broken. Take bottles out first. Breaking it drops every bottle.

# Drink Station levels
- What it is: Four levels of station, Mk I to Mk IV.
- You get: Mk I: brewing stand and storage. Mk II: drinks with 1 effect, 1 Brew Pot, the Latte and the sweetener. Mk III: 2 effects, 2 pots. Mk IV: 3 effects, 3 pots.
- How it works: Open the station and press the Mk button under the brewing info. It lights up when you can afford it.
- How to unlock: Pay 8, 16 and 32 Reinforced Beacon Plating.
- Careful: The storage, the tank and your pot links stay when you upgrade.

# Brew Pot
- What it is: A copper kettle that holds one drink for one person.
- You get: A drink with every effect you mixed, for 10 minutes, plus 10 or 20 minutes of sweetener.
- How it works: Place it within 8 blocks of a Mk II or better station; it links itself. Pick it in the row of pots under the effects, brew into it, then right-click it with a Paper Cup to drink at once. The board shows the drink and its time.
- How to unlock: Craft it from copper, a sign and a cauldron, or buy it at Workshop Fabrication. A station links 1, 2 or 3 pots at Mk II, III and IV.
- Careful: Brewing into a pot that still has a drink asks you first, and the old drink is poured away.

# Cup Dispenser
- What it is: A box of Paper Cups.
- You get: A Paper Cup with one right-click. A message tells you how many are left.
- How it works: To stock it, crouch with BOTH hands empty and right-click. Put up to 64 cups inside. Every drink from a Brew Pot uses up a cup, so keep it stocked.
- How to unlock: Buy it at Workshop Fabrication.
- Careful: It cannot make cups. Breaking it drops its cups.

# Paper Cup
- What it is: A paper cup for drinks.
- You get: Your drink from a Brew Pot, and the base of a Latte.
- How it works: Right-click a full Brew Pot with it to drink. The cup is used up, as it is in a Latte.
- How to unlock: Craft 4 from 3 paper, in the shape of a bowl.

# Latte
- What it is: A drink you carry, like a sandwich.
- You get: Up to 2 effects for 10 minutes, drunk whenever you like. They stack to 16.
- How it works: In the Latte tab, put a Paper Cup in the cup slot and add potions (or press Gather potions), then press Make Latte.
- How to unlock: A Mk II station or better.
- Careful: A Latte takes no sweetener. Mk II makes Lattes with 1 effect.

# Sweetener
- What it is: A tank of syrup made from Regeneration potions.
- You get: More time on a Brew Pot drink: +10 minutes for 1,000 mB, +20 for 2,000 mB.
- How it works: In the Brew Pot tab, put drinkable Regeneration potions in the pink slot after the potions: I adds 250 mB, II adds 750 mB, and you get the bottle back. Its bar shows the tank. Pick +0, +10 or +20 with the button beside it.
- How to unlock: A Mk II station or better.
- Careful: The tank holds 4,000 mB. Only full steps are spent; what is left stays in the tank.

# What a drink does
- What it is: Real potion effects, shown in your usual effect list.
- You get: Every effect you mixed, at the level of its potion (Speed II stays Speed II).
- How it works: The drink's timer runs only in the field. In your base or an active FOB it stops and the effects never run out. Logging out pauses it too.
- How to unlock: Drink from a Brew Pot or drink a Latte.
- Careful: One drink at a time: a new one replaces the old. It sits beside your meal. Dying clears it. The Milk Dispenser and the Milk Bottle clear it; a milk bucket does not.
- Good to know: A stronger potion of the same effect wins while it lasts. Your drink keeps counting and comes back after it.
gui.eternal_defense.guide.drinks.detail:
- Mk I to IV: effects per drink 0/1/2/3; linked Brew Pots 0/1/2/3 within 8 blocks. One potion per effect, never two of the same effect.
- A drink lasts 10 minutes in the field. Sweetener: +10 minutes for 1,000 mB, +20 for 2,000 mB, so 10 to 30 minutes. Tank 4,000 mB; Regeneration I (also the long one) 250 mB, Regeneration II 750 mB.
- A Latte: a Paper Cup plus up to 2 potions (1 at Mk II), 10 minutes, no sweetener, stacks to 16.
- Storage: 54 slots of up to 64 bottles of one potion. Over 256 bottles the station cannot be broken. Shift-click potions in your pack to store them.
- Gather takes the strongest potion of each chosen effect from the storage, then your pack. Take back returns the potions to the storage (your pack when it is full).
- The brewing stand uses one blaze powder for 20 brews; a brew takes 20 seconds. Other mods' brewing recipes work too.
- Paper Cup: 3 paper make 4. Brew Pot: 7 copper ingots, a sign and a cauldron. Drink Station Mk I: planks, 2 iron, 1 glass bottle, a brewing stand and a cauldron.

Station upgrades cost 8/16/32 Reinforced Plating.

gui.eternal_defense.guide.mre.title: MRE Station & MREs
gui.eternal_defense.guide.mre.body:
# MRE Station
- What it is: A ration packer. It packs food you pick into one MRE you can carry.
- You get: An MRE that restores exactly what its foods would, all in one bite, with no effects.
- How it works: Open it. Put up to six different foods in the food slots, Marines Fuel and Paper in the two slots beside them, then press Make MRE. Each MRE takes one of each food, 1 Marines Fuel and 1 Paper.
- How to unlock: Buy it at Workshop Fabrication. Place it inside your zone.
- Careful: One MRE holds at most 20 nutrition. A food that would go past 20 does not fit in a slot.
- Careful: Every effect is lost. A golden apple, honey or suspicious stew gives only its food, and a sandwich loses its meal.
- Good to know: Bowls and bottles come back to your pack, or drop at your feet when it is full. Take back returns everything in the station.

# MRE
- What it is: A sealed field ration.
- You get: The nutrition and saturation of the foods packed into it, all at once. MREs with the same numbers stack to 64.
- How it works: Eat it like any food. It takes less than a second, and only when you are hungry.
- How to unlock: Make it at an MRE Station.
- Good to know: Hover over it to see what it restores. Nothing comes back when you eat it.

# Marines Fuel
- What it is: A wax crayon, the binder that seals an MRE's paper.
- You get: The seal for one MRE per crayon.
- How it works: Put it in the Marines Fuel slot of an MRE Station. Each MRE uses 1.
- How to unlock: Craft 2 from a clay ball and any dye.
- Careful: It is not food.
gui.eternal_defense.guide.mre.detail:
- An MRE holds up to 20 nutrition. Its saturation is the sum of what each food adds when eaten alone (nutrition x saturation modifier x 2), at most 20.
- It is eaten in 16 ticks (0.8 s), only when you are hungry. Your saturation still stops at your hunger level, as with any food.
- Each MRE uses one of each food in the six slots, 1 Marines Fuel and 1 Paper. Effects and always-edible are dropped.
- Marines Fuel: 1 clay ball and 1 dye (any dye) make 2.
- MRE Station: 4 Reinforced Beacon Plating, 8 iron ingots and a smoker at Workshop Fabrication.

gui.eternal_defense.guide.hub.body:
# Logistics Center Hub
- What it is: A big supply depot for your base. It holds 270 stacks of anything.
- You get: One store your whole base can use. When a recipe, an upgrade or a purchase in your zone needs items, they come from your pack first, then from the Hub.
- How it works: Place it inside your zone. It is 3 blocks wide, deep and tall. Open it from any side, put items in, and turn its 5 pages with the arrows.
- How to unlock: Buy it at Workshop Fabrication for 64 Reinforced Beacon Plating, 64 iron ingots, 16 chests and 8 hoppers.
- Careful: It cannot be broken while it holds items. Empty it first, or move it with the Beacon Recovery Shovel: its items wait for it.
- Careful: Outside your zone it does nothing. FOBs never take from it.
- Good to know: While you stand in a zone with a working Hub, the Logistics Hub Zone effect shows. The beacon's Overview says how many Hubs work.
- Good to know: When the Hub pays for something, everyone in your zone sees a chat line with what it gave.
- Good to know: Hoppers and droppers can fill it and empty it from any side.
- Good to know: Create's belts can run straight into it. Funnels, chutes and mechanical arms work on any side too.
gui.eternal_defense.guide.hub.detail:
- The Hub has 270 slots: 5 pages of 54. Items stack as in a chest; an item that does not stack takes a slot of its own.
- Supply order: your pack, then the nearest Hub in your zone, then the next one. A request that cannot be paid in full takes nothing.
- Chat lines name at most 3 kinds of item, then the rest as a count. Pulls by the same player within 2 seconds add up to one line.
- Price: 64 Reinforced Beacon Plating, 64 iron ingots, 16 chests and 8 hoppers.

gui.eternal_defense.guide.loadout.body:
# Loadout Station
- What it is: A big machine for your base. It packs gear into coins and puts a coin’s gear on you.
- You get: Your armor, off hand and hotbar swapped for a saved kit in about six seconds.
- How it works: Right-click the machine to open it. Put gear in the Kit slots and press Make coin. Put the coin in a coin slot, press Set active, then press Print.
- Good to know: Sneak and right-click the machine to print your active coin without opening it.
- How to unlock: Buy it at Workshop Fabrication for 64 Reinforced Beacon Plating, 8 Beacon Restoration Matrices, 32 iron ingots and 16 glass. It is 3 blocks wide, deep and tall.
- Careful: While it prints you, you cannot move, fight or use items. What you wore goes to a Logistics Hub, or to the station’s Locker when no Hub has room.
- Careful: It cannot be broken while coins are in its slots. Take them out first.
- Good to know: The 27 slots of your main inventory are never touched.
- Good to know: The figure on the left wears a kit before you print it. Use the arrows to look through the coin slots, and drag the figure to turn it.
- Good to know: Press sneak or Esc to skip the camera shots. The print goes on.

# Loadout Coin
- What it is: A sealed package of real gear: the 4 armor pieces, the off hand item and the 9 hotbar items, exactly as they were.
- You get: A kit you can print again and again, or hand to a teammate. Anyone can use any coin.
- How it works: Make it at the Loadout Station. Put it in a coin slot, hold it while you step in, or keep coins of the same kind in a Logistics Hub.
- How to unlock: Each coin costs the gear in it, plus 4 Reinforced Beacon Plating and 1 Ardent Energy. The fee comes from your pack first, then from a Hub.
- Careful: A coin cannot hold another coin, or a shulker box, bundle or backpack with things inside.
- Good to know: Identical coins stack up to 16. A coin slot keeps taking only the kind it held until you press Forget.

# Loadout Flare
- What it is: A flare that calls the kit of your active coin slot to you.
- You get: A Loadout Capsule with the kit, fired in by your Support Cannon.
- How it works: Set an active coin slot at the Loadout Station, then throw the flare. The cannon turns, fires, and a capsule slams down by the flare.
- How to unlock: Buy it at your Support Platform for 5 Ardent Energy. You need a Loadout Station and a Support Cannon in your base.
- Careful: The coin is used only when the cannon fires. If the call fails, you keep the flare and the coin.
- Careful: Under 3 or more blocks of cover it needs Quantum tunneling. In other dimensions it needs Dimensional link.

# Loadout Capsule
- What it is: The shell-shaped pod a Loadout Flare brings. Your kit is inside.
- You get: Your kit where you threw the flare, without walking home.
- How it works: It hits the ground hard and opens by itself. Right-click it and press Equip to put every item into its own slot, or take items out by hand.
- How to unlock: Throw a Loadout Flare.
- Careful: Equip only fills empty slots. Nothing is replaced, and the rest stays in the capsule.
- Careful: Only the player who threw the flare can open it.
- Good to know: It lands with a bang, but it breaks no blocks and hurts no one.
- Good to know: Take everything out and it folds away. Where there is no room for it, your kit comes in a supply parcel.
gui.eternal_defense.guide.loadout.detail:

- A coin’s fee: 4 Reinforced Beacon Plating and 1 Ardent Energy. A kit may hold up to 64 KB of item data.
- Loadout Flare: 5 Ardent Energy at the Support Platform. The capsule lands 12 seconds after the cannon fires, or 7 seconds underground.
- To print, stand within 4 blocks of the doors, in front of them, with nothing in the way. You can print again 30 seconds after your last print ends; logging out does not reset it.
- The coin is taken from your coin slot first, then from your main hand, then from a Logistics Hub (only a coin of the same kind).
- An unopened capsule stays for 30 minutes, like a supply parcel, then its kit falls out.

gui.eternal_defense.guide.defense.title: Turrets & Power
gui.eternal_defense.guide.defense.body:
# Defense Depot
- What it is: A shop booth for your base. It sells turrets, turret ammo and defenses for Universal Ammo Coins.
- You get: All nine turrets, the three turret ammo types, Sandbags, Barricades, Barbed Wire, Shock Boxes and Electric Wire.
- How it works: Right-click it, pick a row and press Buy. The coins come from your pack first, then from a Logistics Hub.
- How to unlock: Buy it at Workshop Fabrication, in the Defense group, for 16 iron ingots, 8 copper ingots, 2 chests and 2 Reinforced Beacon Plating.
- Careful: Every piece of defense gear stands only inside your beacon zone or inside a FOB's zone.
- Good to know: It is 2 blocks wide and 2 tall.

# Shaft Dynamo and Cog Dynamo
- What it is: Two Create machines that turn Create rotation into power for your defenses.
- You get: A base for a Power Pole. A pole on a turning dynamo feeds a power network.
- How it works: Run a Create shaft into a side of the Shaft Dynamo, or set a Create cogwheel beside the Cog Dynamo's cog. Then place a Power Pole on top.
- How to unlock: Buy them at Workshop Fabrication, in the Defense group, for 16 copper ingots, 8 iron ingots, 8 andesite alloy and 4 redstone each.
- Careful: Turrets and Shock Boxes put stress on the Create network that turns the dynamo. If that network is overstressed, the whole power network goes down.
- Good to know: A dynamo makes power at 8 RPM or more. The faster it turns, the more stress the same defenses ask. Several dynamos in one network share the load.
- Good to know: Every side of the Shaft Dynamo turns the same way as the shaft that drives it, so a shaft line can run straight through.
- Good to know: Right-click a dynamo with an empty hand, or look at it wearing Engineer's Goggles. It says if it works, how many stress units it carries and how many its whole power network asks.

# Power Pole
- What it is: A pole 2 blocks tall that carries power.
- You get: Turrets within 8 blocks of a powered pole work by themselves.
- How it works: Place it on a dynamo to start a network. Place more poles further out and join them with Electric Wire to carry the power on. Right-click a pole to read its network.
- How to unlock: Buy it at Workshop Fabrication, in the Defense group, for 6 iron ingots and 8 copper ingots.
- Good to know: A pole reaches 4 blocks down and 6 blocks up. A turret takes its power from the nearest pole that reaches it.
- Good to know: Hold any defense gear, like a turret, a pole or Electric Wire, and every pole near you shows its reach as see-through walls with an outline: blue when it has power, orange when its network is down. A pole in your hand shows where its reach would be.
- Good to know: Sneak and right-click a pole with both hands empty to keep its walls on all the time. Do it again to hide it.

# Electric Wire
- What it is: Copper cable for your power network.
- You get: Power carried from pole to pole, from a pole to a Shock Box, and from a Shock Box to Barbed Wire.
- How it works: Right-click the first block with the wire, then the second. Each span uses one wire. Sneak and right-click a pole or Shock Box to take its wires off; they drop back as items.
- How to unlock: Buy 8 for 16 Universal Ammo Coins at the Defense Depot, or craft 4 from 2 copper ingots and 1 string.
- Careful: A span is at most 16 blocks long.

# Shock Box
- What it is: A battery box that makes Barbed Wire live.
- You get: Live Barbed Wire, which hurts more and slows hard.
- How it works: Wire a powered Power Pole to the box, then wire the box to a Barbed Wire block. The Barbed Wire joined to that block goes live too, up to 15 blocks, like a redstone signal.
- How to unlock: Buy it at the Defense Depot for 64 Universal Ammo Coins.
- Careful: It puts 8 stress per RPM on the network, like a small turret.
- Careful: One box makes at most 15 Barbed Wire blocks live, the nearest first. Use more boxes for longer lines.
- Good to know: When the power goes down, its charge keeps the wire live for 30 more seconds.

# Machine Gun Turrets
- What it is: Automatic machine guns in three Marks: Light Gun Turret, Machine Gun Turret and Twin Machine Gun Turret.
- You get: Fast fire at hostile mobs and raiders, 18, 22 and 26 blocks out.
- How it works: Place it where a powered Power Pole reaches it and load Turret MG Ammo. It finds a target, turns and fires by itself.
- How to unlock: Buy them at the Defense Depot for 96, 192 and 384 Universal Ammo Coins.
- Careful: Raiders adapt. Turret bullets count as a projectile trap, so raiders shrug them off more with every wave you use them.
- Good to know: The Twin Machine Gun Turret is 2 by 2 blocks and 2 tall. The others are 1 block wide and 2 tall.
- Good to know: The lamp above every turret shows how it stands: green when it is ready, orange when it is out of ammo, red when no power reaches it. Look at a turret to read the same in words.

# Shotgun Turrets
- What it is: Turrets that fire a spread of pellets: Shotgun Turret, Auto-Shotgun Turret and Twin Auto-Shotgun Turret.
- You get: Heavy damage up close, 10, 12 and 14 blocks out. One shot can hit several mobs. Each shot pushes every mob it hits back a little.
- How it works: Place it where a powered Power Pole reaches it and load Turret Shotgun Shells.
- How to unlock: Buy them at the Defense Depot for 96, 192 and 384 Universal Ammo Coins.
- Careful: Pellets count as a projectile trap, like bullets, so raiders adapt to both.

# Flame Turrets
- What it is: Flamethrower turrets: Flame Turret, Heavy Flame Turret and Twin Flame Turret.
- You get: A jet of fire 8, 10 and 12 blocks long and 2, 2.5 and 3 blocks wide that burns every hostile mob in it.
- How it works: Place it where a powered Power Pole reaches it and load Turret Flame Fuel.
- How to unlock: Buy them at the Defense Depot for 128, 256 and 512 Universal Ammo Coins.
- Careful: Fire-proof mobs do not burn. Raiders adapt to fire like any other trap.
- Good to know: A wall or block in the way cuts the jet short.

# Turret ammo
- What it is: Turret MG Ammo, Turret Shotgun Shells and Turret Flame Fuel. Each turret takes only its own kind.
- You get: 64 shots a can, 12 shots a box and 40 bursts a bottle.
- How it works: Right-click a turret with its ammo in hand. Or right-click it with anything else to open its screen and put ammo in its four slots yourself.
- How it works: A hopper, a Create chute or a Create funnel feeds it too. A Create belt feeds it through a funnel on the turret.
- How to unlock: Buy 4 at the Defense Depot for 32, 32 and 40 Universal Ammo Coins, or make them with Create.
- Good to know: MG Ammo: press 4 cartridge cases, 2 propellant and 1 iron ingot in a basin.
- Good to know: Shotgun Shells: press 2 cartridge cases, 2 propellant, 3 iron nuggets and 1 paper in a basin.
- Good to know: Flame Fuel: mix a glass bottle, 2 coal or charcoal and 1 propellant in a heated basin.
- Good to know: Take ammo back out in the turret's screen. Hoppers and Create only put ammo in. Breaking the turret drops its ammo.

# Sandbags
- What it is: A wall of sandbags that joins up like a stone wall.
- You get: Cover that raiders' arrows and bullets barely scratch.
- How it works: Build a line of it. Raiders go for defenses first, so it holds them up while your turrets fire.
- How to unlock: Buy 8 for 16 Universal Ammo Coins at the Defense Depot.
- Careful: Raiders' blows hurt it as much as any other block.

# Barricade
- What it is: A timber and steel barricade that joins up like a fence.
- You get: A wall that raiders' blows barely dent.
- How it works: Build a line of it where raiders come in to fight it up close.
- How to unlock: Buy 4 for 16 Universal Ammo Coins at the Defense Depot.
- Careful: Raiders' shots hurt it as much as any other block.

# Barbed Wire
- What it is: Low coils of wire that you can walk into but not quickly through.
- You get: Everything in it is slowed. A hostile mob in it, or hitting it, is cut for 2 damage.
- How it works: Lay it where raiders come in. Wire a Shock Box to it to make it live: then it shocks for 5 damage and slows mobs hard.
- How to unlock: Buy 8 for 16 Universal Ammo Coins at the Defense Depot.
- Careful: It has little health, so raiders break it fast.
- Careful: Raiders adapt to its cuts and shocks like any trap. Players are slowed but never hurt.
gui.eternal_defense.guide.defense.detail:
- Turret range: machine gun 18, 22 and 26 blocks, shotgun 10, 12 and 14, flame 8, 10 and 12 (Mark I, II and III).
- Damage a second on one target: machine gun 8, 14 and 21.3, shotgun 7.5, 14 and 27.2 when every pellet hits, and each shot knocks a mob back an eighth, three sixteenths and a quarter as hard as a punch (Mark I, II and III), flame 12, 16 and 20 on each mob in the jet, plus 5, 6 and 7 seconds of fire. The jet is 2, 2.5 and 3 blocks wide.
- Stress per RPM: machine gun and shotgun 8, 12 and 20, flame 12, 16 and 24, Shock Box 8. Create multiplies it by the dynamo's speed.
- A dynamo makes power from 8 RPM. A pole reaches 8 blocks around, 4 down and 6 up. A span of wire is at most 16 blocks. A pole holds 8 spans and a Shock Box 4.
- A turret holds 4 stacks of its ammo. Sandbags take a quarter of the damage from shots, a Barricade 40%% from blows.
- A Shock Box charge lasts 30 seconds and makes up to 15 joined Barbed Wire blocks live. Live wire slows for 2 seconds.
